title: To Fire, Giver of Good Things

plan.english: Now, Fire, we call upon you at the sacrifice. You indeed are the giver of good things, the guest of men. You who were born from the wood carry what is poured to the sky. Now your tongue licks the butter. Hear our hymn, immortal one! Give us cattle, swift horses and sons. May our fame indeed be imperishable.

clauses.english: Now, Fire, we call upon you at the sacrifice.
You indeed are the giver of good things, the guest of men.
You who were born from the wood carry what is poured to the sky.
Now your tongue licks the butter.
Hear our hymn, immortal one!
Give us cattle, swift horses and sons.
May our fame indeed be imperishable.

plan.english: Fire, you go between Sky and Earth. You carry the word to the gods. You indeed bring them to our sacrifice. You who know the paths of the gods, guard our house. Now lead them here, bright one. And seat them at our hearth.

clauses.english: Fire, you go between Sky and Earth.
You carry the word to the gods.
You indeed bring them to our sacrifice.
You who know the paths of the gods, guard our house.
Now lead them here, bright one.
And seat them at our hearth.

plan.english: Now we praise Fire, the young god. He was born in the dry wood, and he grew in the night. Then he rose up to the sky; his light became bright for men. The immortals saw and rejoiced. May he burn in the house for a long lifetime.

clauses.english: Now we praise Fire, the young god.
He was born in the dry wood, and he grew in the night.
Then he rose up to the sky; his light became bright for men.
The immortals saw and rejoiced.
May he burn in the house for a long lifetime.

plan.english: Now come, immortal gods, to our feast! We have spread the seats, we have poured the sweet mead. Sit down, taste, and rejoice! Whoever pours for you, to him give good things.

clauses.english: Now come, immortal gods, to our feast!
We have spread the seats, we have poured the sweet mead.
Sit down, taste, and rejoice!
Whoever pours for you, to him give good things.

plan.english: Father Sky, hear our hymn! To you indeed let us pour the mead. To you indeed let us burn the fat. Father, you see the deeds of men from above. Pour rain upon the wide earth. Let our grain grow, and let our livestock grow.

clauses.english: Father Sky, hear our hymn!
To you indeed let us pour the mead.
To you indeed let us burn the fat.
Father, you see the deeds of men from above.
Pour rain upon the wide earth.
Let our grain grow, and let our livestock grow.

plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, has come. And in the morning we have kindled the fire. The bright fire woke up with the Dawn. Dawn and Fire light up the earth. Dawn and Fire, protect our people!

clauses.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, has come.
And in the morning we have kindled the fire.
The bright fire woke up with the Dawn.
Dawn and Fire light up the earth.
Dawn and Fire, protect our people!

plan.english: Sweet mead, delight of the deities! You were born from honey in the cauldron. Gods and men drink you, dear one. You are the great joy of the immortals. Now let us pour the first share for the gods. Then let us drink you from full cups.

clauses.english: Sweet mead, delight of the deities!
You were born from honey in the cauldron.
Gods and men drink you, dear one.
You are the great joy of the immortals.
Now let us pour the first share for the gods.
Then let us drink you from full cups.

plan.english: Now we sing of Perkunos, the strong god. And he drank the mead from a great cup. His heart became glad, and he became strong. Then he slew the serpent and freed the waters. And the waters flowed down to the earth. May Perkunos drink this mead. May he slay the enemies of our people.

clauses.english: Now we sing of Perkunos, the strong god.
And he drank the mead from a great cup.
His heart became glad, and he became strong.
Then he slew the serpent and freed the waters.
And the waters flowed down to the earth.
May Perkunos drink this mead.
May he slay the enemies of our people.

title: To the Fire of the Hearth

plan.english: Now, Fire of the hearth, you sit in our house. You warm the old men and the children, shining one. You cook our food; in the night you guard us. We give you butter and dry wood. Do not die, bright fire, shining one!

clauses.english: Now, Fire of the hearth, you sit in our house.
You warm the old men and the children, shining one.
You cook our food; in the night you guard us.
We give you butter and dry wood.
Do not die, bright fire, shining one!

plan.english: Nebhtus, master of the water, hear! To you we have poured the warm milk. You who dwell in the river, receive our gift. May our livestock drink your water. Do not seize our sons in the river.

clauses.english: Nebhtus, master of the water, hear!
To you we have poured the warm milk.
You who dwell in the river, receive our gift.
May our livestock drink your water.
Do not seize our sons in the river.

plan.english: The tongue of the fire indeed is red. It licks the fat; it devours the meat. Its black smoke rises upward. The gods smell the smoke and come. May Fire burn for the immortals.

clauses.english: The tongue of the fire indeed is red.
It licks the fat; it devours the meat.
Its black smoke rises upward.
The gods smell the smoke and come.
May Fire burn for the immortals.

plan.english: We sing a new hymn to the immortals. Our song is sweet and dear. Gods, hear the word of our mouth! Your name indeed is famous; your fame is great. Give good fame to the man who sings.

clauses.english: We sing a new hymn to the immortals.
Our song is sweet and dear.
Gods, hear the word of our mouth!
Your name indeed is famous; your fame is great.
Give good fame to the man who sings.

plan.english: Now, Bhagos, you give the people their shares. You gave the first share to the gods. For you, Bhagos, we prepare the feast. Sit down at our hearth; give us a great gift. Giver of good things, we praise you with a hymn.

clauses.english: Now, Bhagos, you give the people their shares.
You gave the first share to the gods.
For you, Bhagos, we prepare the feast.
Sit down at our hearth; give us a great gift.
Giver of good things, we praise you with a hymn.

plan.english: Evening has come, and the sun has sunk. And now, shining one, you light up the house in the night. Guard us through the dark night. And drive the wolf away from our sheep. At dawn let us pour the butter.

clauses.english: Evening has come, and the sun has sunk.
And now, shining one, you light up the house in the night.
Guard us through the dark night.
And drive the wolf away from our sheep.
At dawn let us pour the butter.

plan.english: Mother Earth, Father Sky! You two have given grain, cattle and sheep. For you we have poured the mead; take this poured offering. Now be dear to us, and guard our children.

clauses.english: Mother Earth, Father Sky!
You two have given grain, cattle and sheep.
For you we have poured the mead; take this poured offering.
Now be dear to us, and guard our children.

title: At the Pouring of the Mead

plan.english: God, drink this sweet mead! We have poured it for you from the full cauldron. Now become glad, and be dear to us.

clauses.english: God, drink this sweet mead!
We have poured it for you from the full cauldron.
Now become glad, and be dear to us.

plan.english: Burn, fire; burn, bright one! Guard our house; do not burn it! Burn the dry wood; become bright!

clauses.english: Burn, fire; burn, bright one!
Guard our house; do not burn it!
Burn the dry wood; become bright!

plan.english: Now, Bhagos, protect our cattle from the wolf! And may our cows give much milk. And may the wolf not seize our sheep. We give you this fat.

clauses.english: Now, Bhagos, protect our cattle from the wolf!
And may our cows give much milk.
And may the wolf not seize our sheep.
We give you this fat.

plan.english: Now, Dawn, give me a son! May he be strong and wise and famous. And may his fame be great. Now I have poured the sweet mead for you.

clauses.english: Now, Dawn, give me a son!
May he be strong and wise and famous.
And may his fame be great.
Now I have poured the sweet mead for you.

plan.english: Bhagos, be satisfied with the sacrifice. For you indeed we burned fat. For you we poured out the new mead. Now take the sacrifice and give us good things.

clauses.english: Bhagos, be satisfied with the sacrifice.
For you indeed we burned fat.
For you we poured out the new mead.
Now take the sacrifice and give us good things.

plan.english: God, give us a long lifetime. May we live; may we see the sun. May the children see many days.

clauses.english: God, give us a long lifetime.
May we live; may we see the sun.
May the children see many days.

plan.english: Let me pour the first share for the god. Let me drink the mead from the full cup. And may the mead be sweet in our mouths.

clauses.english: Let me pour the first share for the god.
Let me drink the mead from the full cup.
And may the mead be sweet in our mouths.

plan.english: Now, gods, hear our word! Now we call you with a hymn. Come to the sacrifice, sit down by the fire. Become glad; be kindly to us.

clauses.english: Now, gods, hear our word!
Now we call you with a hymn.
Come to the sacrifice, sit down by the fire.
Become glad; be kindly to us.

plan.english: Now I have poured water on the fields. Perkunos, pour rain on the fields! May the rivers flow, may the grain grow.

clauses.english: Now I have poured water on the fields.
Perkunos, pour rain on the fields!
May the rivers flow, may the grain grow.

plan.english: Now I have lain down near the fire. Now, bright one, guard me in the night. May the enemy not come to our village. At dawn let me kindle you, shining one.

clauses.english: Now I have lain down near the fire.
Now, bright one, guard me in the night.
May the enemy not come to our village.
At dawn let me kindle you, shining one.

plan.english: Now, fire, burn our enemies! Burn their house, burn their fields. May they not see us; now protect our people.

clauses.english: Now, fire, burn our enemies!
Burn their house, burn their fields.
May they not see us; now protect our people.

plan.english: Now we have poured milk for you, shining one. Drink the warm milk, bright one. May the cows be many and healthy.

clauses.english: Now we have poured milk for you, shining one.
Drink the warm milk, bright one.
May the cows be many and healthy.

title: For the Guest at the Feast

plan.english: Dear guest, sit down on the seat. Eat the meat, guest, drink the mead. May the gods give you good things; be dear to us.

clauses.english: Dear guest, sit down on the seat.
Eat the meat, guest, drink the mead.
May the gods give you good things; be dear to us.

plan.english: At dawn stand up and wash your hands. Put dry wood on the fire-altar. Kindle the fire and praise it. When it has become bright, sing the hymn. Then pour butter into the fire.

clauses.english: At dawn stand up and wash your hands.
Put dry wood on the fire-altar.
Kindle the fire and praise it.
When it has become bright, sing the hymn.
Then pour butter into the fire.

plan.english: Pour fat into the fire three times. Then pour mead for Perkunos, and pour water for the dead. Put barley and grain on the fire. May the smoke rise upward.

clauses.english: Pour fat into the fire three times.
Then pour mead for Perkunos, and pour water for the dead.
Put barley and grain on the fire.
May the smoke rise upward.

plan.english: Lead the ram to the altar. Slit it open with the knife. Pour out its blood on the earth. Cook the meat on spits. Give the first share to the god, and burn the fat in the fire. Then let the people eat the meat.

clauses.english: Lead the ram to the altar.
Slit it open with the knife.
Pour out its blood on the earth.
Cook the meat on spits.
Give the first share to the god, and burn the fat in the fire.
Then let the people eat the meat.

plan.english: Put honey and water in the cauldron. Heat the cauldron at the fire. Let it boil for three days. Then pour out the mead. Do not drink the first cup; give it to the god.

clauses.english: Put honey and water in the cauldron.
Heat the cauldron at the fire.
Let it boil for three days.
Then pour out the mead.
Do not drink the first cup; give it to the god.

plan.english: Whoever pours, let him give the first cup to the gods. Then let the old man drink; then let the young men sip. Whoever does not pour, may Perkunos not listen to him.

clauses.english: Whoever pours, let him give the first cup to the gods.
Then let the old man drink; then let the young men sip.
Whoever does not pour, may Perkunos not listen to him.

plan.english: Spread the seats around the fire. There the gods sit. Do not sit down on their seats. Set the cups in front of the seats. Fill them with milk.

clauses.english: Spread the seats around the fire.
There the gods sit.
Do not sit down on their seats.
Set the cups in front of the seats.
Fill them with milk.

plan.english: Wash your hands; then pour the libation. Do not urinate toward the sun, nor into the river. Do not step over the hearth. Whoever does these things, Perkunos is angry at him.

clauses.english: Wash your hands; then pour the libation.
Do not urinate toward the sun, nor into the river.
Do not step over the hearth.
Whoever does these things, Perkunos is angry at him.

plan.english: Milk the cow at dawn. Heat the milk at the fire. Pour it warm into the fire. Give the remainder to the dog.

clauses.english: Milk the cow at dawn.
Heat the milk at the fire.
Pour it warm into the fire.
Give the remainder to the dog.

plan.english: When the gods have eaten, let us eat the meat. Let us drink the mead and sing the songs. Let the old men tell the stories of their fathers. Whoever is sad, let him become glad.

clauses.english: When the gods have eaten, let us eat the meat.
Let us drink the mead and sing the songs.
Let the old men tell the stories of their fathers.
Whoever is sad, let him become glad.

plan.english: If a guest comes to the sacrifice, give him a seat and a share. Give him food from the cauldron. Whoever drives away a guest, may Bhagos not hear him.

clauses.english: If a guest comes to the sacrifice, give him a seat and a share.
Give him food from the cauldron.
Whoever drives away a guest, may Bhagos not hear him.

plan.english: Guard the fire of the hearth. Let it not die in the night. In the evening cover it. At dawn put new wood on it. If it dies, seek new fire in the household of the king. Carry it home in a pot.

clauses.english: Guard the fire of the hearth.
Let it not die in the night.
In the evening cover it.
At dawn put new wood on it.
If it dies, seek new fire in the household of the king.
Carry it home in a pot.

plan.english: When the guests have eaten, pour out the remainder for the dead. Praise them with a song. Leave the altar, go home, and rejoice.

clauses.english: When the guests have eaten, pour out the remainder for the dead.
Praise them with a song.
Leave the altar, go home, and rejoice.
